sentences: Detecting a k-vertex independent set means determining whether a graph contains k mutually nonadjacent vertices.
The question asks for the round complexity of this task in CONGEST, where processors communicate only along actual graph edges with bounded-size messages.
In centralized computation, complementing the graph converts the task to clique detection.
That conversion does not preserve a distributed communication network, because absent edges cannot simply become communication links.

Understanding the complexity would expose how distributed pattern detection depends on the difference between information about missing edges and the physical routes available for exchanging that information.
